newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Utilities up after offer for HK Electric.
newsitem.headline: Utilities up after offer for HK Electric.

text.p: Utilities shares rose following news that Hutchison Whampoa Ltd would make a conditional cash offer for all Hongkong Electric Holdings Ltd shares at premium, brokers said on Monday.
"The news is seen to be positive," said Alex Wong, research analyst at Dharmala Securities. "It has fueled short term demand for utilities counters such as China Light."
"As the offer is at a premium, it has led to an expectation that inactive utilities stocks deserve a higher price, and that boosts demand," one sales director at a regional brokerage said.
Shares of China Light & Power Co Ltd rose HK$1.00 to HK$35 in late morning with 4.82 million shares traded.
Brokers said talk of a possible covered warrant issue on China Light also boosted demand for the stock.
Among other utilities, Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd edged up HK$0.20 to HK$12.50, and Hong Kong and China Gas Co Ltd advanced HK$0.20 to HK$15 per share.
The Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd group, including Cheung Kong Infrastructure Holidings Ltd, Hutchison and Hongkong Electric, announced earlier on Monday of a major corporate reshuffling.
The reorganisation includes a general offer by Hutchison on Hongkong Electric at HK$26.50 each compared to the shares' closing price of HK$25.25 on Friday.
Trading in shares of Hongkong Electric, Hutchison, Cheung Kong and Cheung Kong Infrastructure were suspended on Monday.
